r3.texte: Last summer, I stayed with my aunt in a small village near the sea. Every morning I woke up early and walked on the beach with her dog, Max. In the afternoon I helped my aunt in her garden, where she grows tomatoes and flowers. On Fridays there was a market in the village, and we bought fresh fish for dinner. I was sad when the holiday ended, but my aunt promised that I can come back next year.

q.p: Where did the writer stay?
What did she do in the morning?
o: She walked on the beach with a dog

q.p: What did they buy on Fridays?
How did the writer feel at the end?

r3.texte: Many people think that working from home is easy, but Clara, a graphic designer, disagrees. "At first I loved staying in my pyjamas," she says, "but after a month I felt lonely, and I worked far too long." Now she follows a strict timetable: she starts at nine, takes a proper lunch break, and finishes at six. She also rents a desk in a shared office twice a week, where she can meet other freelancers. "I am more creative when I see people," she explains. "And on days at home, I make sure to go for a walk before I start."

q.p: What did Clara find difficult about working at home?
o: Feeling alone and working too much

q.p: What does she do now?
o: Works only in a shared office
Follows a timetable and sometimes uses a shared office

q.p: Why does she rent a desk?
What does the writer say about walks?
o: She goes for one before work on home days
She walks to the office every day
